title: Attesting Biases and Discrimination using Language Semantics
benchmark_measurement: The paper discusses the Implicit-Association Test (IAT) as a tool to measure 'religious implicit biases towards homosexuality' and 'implicit prejudices based on religious ethnicity'. It proposes that similar attestations can be made for AI models by analyzing language semantics.
religious_groups: Homosexuality (in the context of religious bias)
findings: The paper cites previous psychological studies (e.g., IAT) which have successfully measured religious implicit biases towards homosexuality and prejudices based on religious ethnicity. It argues that these human biases are embedded in language corpora and can be inherited and perpetuated by AI systems that train on this data, suggesting that computational methods can attest these biases in AI.
